sentences.text:
Since all the three applications arise out of same Case Crime no. 224 of 2018, u/s 147, 148, 307,
504, 506, 325, 376, 511 I.P.C., they are being heard and decided together.

2. Heard learned counsel for the applicants, learned AGA for the State and perused the papers on record.
3.

The present application has been moved by the applicants, namely, Sumit, Pappu and Naresh,
seeking anticipatory bail in Case Crime no. 224 of 2018, u/s 147, 148, 307, 504, 506, 325, 376, 511 I.P.C., P.S. B.B. Nagar, District Bulandshahar.

4. As per prosecution case, the present applicants along with others came armed with weapons like lathi-danda and country made pistol and began using foul and abusive language against the sister-in-law of the first informant complaining that they illegally broke the med of their fields; they began to attack and physically assault her.
When she tried to escape, one of them Pappu caught hold of her from behind, tore her cloths and attempted to rape her.
On their loud cries, the co-villagers rushed to the spot and saved them.
5. It is contended on behalf of the applicants that the F.I.R. contains false and fabricated facts.
No incident of attempt to rape ever took place.
The other facts are also concocted one.
They are innocent and have been implicated out of enmity.

It is further contended that the applicants took shelter of the High Court and filed a criminal misc. writ petition No. 22886 of 2018 and were given relief that they shall not be arrested in this case till submission of police report u/s 173(2) Cr.P.C.
6.
The anticipatory bail application is ardently opposed by the learned A.G.A. on the premise that the applicants are in the habit of not following the directions of this Court.
It is pointed out that in this case, the charge sheet has been filed on 8.12.2018.
Admittedly, they were granted protection by this Court till submission of charge sheet only.
The applicants very well knew that the charge-sheet has been filed almost three years ago, but they are yet to appear before the court below.
This conduct of theirs disentitle them from grant of this discretionary relief.

7. My attention has also been drawn to an order of this Court in an application u/s 482 No. 15739 of 2020 (Pappu and 4 others vs. State of U.P. and another) wherein the application was disposed of with the direction to the court below to extend the benefit of interim bail if the court concerned deems it fit as contemplated in the law laid down in Lal Kamlendra Pratap Singh vs. State of U.P.,
2009 (3) ADJ 322 (SC), if the applicants surrender within 30 days from the date of the order.

entities.text:
Lal Kamlendra Pratap Singh vs. State of U.P.,
2009 (3) ADJ 322 (SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the basis of the above direction of the Court, it is argued that the applicants have been avoiding the process of law by applying for simultaneous relief in different forums of the Court and that their conduct is not condonable.

Besides above, it is argued that the applicants are named in the F.I.R.
The victim in this case, namely, Badan Singh, sustained a number of injuries including fracture of ribs No. 6 & 7.
Sumit vs State Of U.P. on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14169649/
2 8.
It may also be kept in mind that anticipatory bail is an extraordinary remedy to be exercised in suitable cases only.

This discretionary power calls for existence of facts of the kind where the court is satisfied that its interference is necessary to further the cause of justice and to prevent misuse of process of law.
In the instant case this fact cannot simply be ignored that applicants did not surrender before the court concerned despite clear direction to do so.
9. In view of the facts and circumstances of the case I do not find it a fit case for grant of benefit of anticipatory bail.
10. Hence the anticipatory bail application is rejected.

11. It is made clear that observations made in rejecting anticipatory bail to the applicants shall not,
in any way, affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on material before him, at any stage of the case.
